body.zh-Hant: 據波蘭國家記憶研究院（IPN）的傳記，托梅（Wiktor Thommée）生於維爾諾地區的申奇揚尼（Święciany），家族有法國淵源。1924年他晉升准將（gen. brygady），接掌駐比得哥什的第15步兵師；該師師長之職一直擔任到1934年，之後轉任托倫第VIII軍區司令，1938年再任羅茲第IV軍區司令。
body.en: According to the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), Wiktor Thommée was born in Święciany in the Vilnius region into a family of French roots. In 1924 he was promoted to brigadier general and took over the 15th Infantry Division in Bydgoszcz; he kept that post until 1934, when he became chief of Corps District No. VIII in Toruń, and in 1938 of Corps District No. IV in Łódź.

heading.zh-Hant: 從皮奧特庫夫集群到羅茲軍殘部
heading.en: From Group Piotrków to the remnants of Army Łódź

body.zh-Hant: 1939年9月1日，托梅接掌「皮奧特庫夫」作戰集群（GO „Piotrków”）。9月7日，羅茲軍原司令羅梅爾（Juliusz Rómmel）離開部隊，托梅隨即接掌羅茲軍的殘部。IPN 記載，他在9月13日抵達莫德林要塞並接下防務。
body.en: On 1 September 1939 Thommée took command of Operational Group „Piotrków”. On 7 September Army „Łódź” commander Juliusz Rómmel left his units, and Thommée then took over what remained of the army. The IPN states that he reached the Modlin fortress on 13 September and took over its defence.

heading.zh-Hant: 莫德林要塞的防禦與投降

body.zh-Hant: IPN 稱他接管要塞時麾下約1.5萬人，其後最大的難題是彈藥將盡；因華沙已投降，繼續作戰失去意義，他於9月29日交出要塞，並談成體面的投降條件。美國陸軍戰史（Kennedy）稱他為莫德林守軍指揮官，並載他把投降歸因於水源被切斷等因素；2.4萬名波軍在莫德林放下武器。
body.en: The IPN says he had about 15,000 men under his orders, and that the greatest problem was dwindling ammunition. With Warsaw having capitulated, further fighting made no sense, and on 29 September he surrendered the fortress, having negotiated honourable terms. The US Army study (Kennedy) calls him commander of the Modlin force, says he attributed the surrender to factors including the cut-off water supply, and records that 24,000 Polish troops laid down their arms there.

heading.en: Captivity, postwar years and posthumous promotion

body.zh-Hant: IPN 記載，1939年11月蓋世太保逮捕了他，他被關進戰俘營（oflag）。直到1956年他才領到軍人退休金；他於1962年11月13日在華沙去世，1964年1月，流亡政府總統扎萊斯基（August Zaleski）追晉他為師級上將（generał dywizji）。
body.en: The IPN records that in November 1939 the Gestapo arrested him and he ended up in an oflag. Only in 1956 did he receive a military pension; he died in Warsaw on 13 November 1962, and in January 1964 the president in exile, August Zaleski, posthumously promoted him to generał dywizji.
